subject: How to estimate Probability of Incidence greater 1 per 10000 population

messages.author: 5b42cf79c787b883
messages.subject: How to estimate Probability of Incidence greater 1 per 10000 population
parts:
Hi all,

I am fitting a spatio-temporal interaction model with negative binomial likelihood using r-INLA with Leroux prior for space and Rw1 for time. I have included environmental covariates (Xit, i=1,2,...s; t=1,2,....t) as fixed effects and ‘O’ the observed case counts as dependent variable in the model. The negative binomial mean is parameterized as,

Mean = r * E,

where ‘r’ is the relative risk and

E is the expected incidence = ratio of observed ‘O’ in a month in an area to cumulative no. of cases for all the months in a year * population of the area.

 I have used the following r-script for fitting the model:

f <- O ~ X1 + X2 + X3 + X4 + X5 + X6 + X7 + X8 +

                f(ID.area,

                   model="besag",

                   graph=Qs,

                   constr=TRUE,

                    rankdef=1,

                    hyper=list(prec=list(prior=sdunif))) +

                    f(ID.month,

                    model="rw1",

                     constr=TRUE,

                     rankdef=1,

                    hyper=list(prec=list(prior=sdunif))) +

                     f(ID.area.month,

                    model="generic0",

                    Cmatrix=R,

                    rankdef=r.def,

                    hyper=list(prec=list(prior=sdunif)),

                     constr=TRUE,

                     extraconstr=list(A=Bst, e=rep(0,nrow(Bst)))) 

 

Model <- inla(f,

                family = "nbinomial",

                  data = data,

                  E=E,

                 control.fixed= list(prec.intercept = 1, prec=1),

                 control.inla = list(tolerance=1e-6, strategy =strategy, int.strategy = "eb", cmin=0), 

                 control.compute=list(dic=TRUE, waic=TRUE, cpo = TRUE, config = TRUE), 

                 control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE, cdf=c(log(1))),

                  verbose = TRUE)

 

Having fitted the model, I understand that the function “cdf=clog(1)” estimates the exceedance probability for relative risk >1. However, I am interested to know the areas in which probability of incidence > 1 per 10,000 populations. I would appreciate if anyone can help me calculating the Prob(incidence >1 per 10000 populations)?

 

Thank you very much!

Uma maheswari.R

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How to estimate Probability of Incidence greater 1 per 10000 population
parts:
I guess if you know the ``expected'' population size you can do that.

' > 1' is 1-(Prob(0) + Prob(1))

so if you know the posterior for the linear predictor, you can simulate
from that one to estimate Prob(0) and Prob(1), and then you have it as
above.

the '10000' corresponds to the scaling 'E', as you have to adjust E
depending on this, like setting E=10000, when you estimate the
probabilities above. (if your 'E' is in ``number of people'' or similar)

Try this out with Poisson data first and a simple model.

parts:
something like this? please check

data(Germany)
g = system.file("demodata/germany.graph", package="INLA")
source(system.file("demodata/Bym-map.R", package="INLA"))
summary(Germany)

## just make a duplicated column
Germany = cbind(Germany,region.struct=Germany$region)

# standard BYM model
formula1 = Y ~ f(region.struct,model="besag",graph=g) +
f(region,model="iid")

result1 = inla(formula1,family="poisson",data=Germany,E=E,
control.compute = list(config = TRUE))


xx <- inla.posterior.sample(1000, result1)


fun <- function(newE) {
return (1-ppois(1, lambda = newE * exp(Predictor)))
}
p.est <- rowMeans( inla.posterior.sample.eval(fun, xx, newE = 1.2) )
